**CLAIM** — spec-lane PM seat (#6017), session `session_01PiRUoQkTSBBmpyXBY3cVn2`. Branch: `claude/issue-7327-settings-visible-grammar`. Dispatching a **cloud dev session** (model: Opus — direction settled by measurement, 1-vs-93→0; the card is a well-bounded schema-narrowing with the grammar spelled out verbatim).

Direction **(b)** as recorded — narrow the declared type, do not touch evaluation: the two `visible` slots (`packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts`, specifier-level and manifest-level — re-anchor by content, the card's `:234`/`:491` may drift) are narrowed to NAME the grammar the save-time evaluator actually implements post-PR #7310 (single root `data`, one-level member access, `|| && !`, `=== !== == != >= <= > <`, string/number/bool/null literals, `${…}` wrapping, bare-string and `{dialect, source}` envelope both accepted) — so an author writing real CEL (`data.x in [...]`) is refused at publish with a prescription naming the supported grammar, and the save-time refusal stays as defense in depth. Aligned with #7071's ruling ("each protocol keeps its own spelling") which named this narrowing as the substantive follow-up.

Premise-first guards: verify PR #7310 is merged on `main` and its "every bundled manifest predicate parses" regression pin exists; re-run the corpus check — all 94 bundled predicates must pass the narrowed declaration (expected 0 refusals post-#7310). If any bundled predicate would newly refuse, STOP and report. Acceptance-face change ⇒ four-step regen (build spec first), authorable-surface/check:generated convergence, changeset level judged from precedent (narrowing acceptance on an authorable key — read #6188/#6815-class precedents and justify).
